$comment: Advisories the CI security gate is allowed to ignore. See scripts/audit-gate.mjs.
An entry belongs here ONLY when there is no published fix to upgrade or
override to, AND the vulnerable code path is unreachable from this app.
If a patched version exists, pin it via `overrides` in package.json instead —
Every entry needs an `expires` date. On that date the gate starts failing
again, forcing a re-evaluation. That is deliberate: this file must not become
a place where advisories go to be forgotten.

allow.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
reason: No published fix exists. The vulnerable range is `<= 3.0.3` and 3.0.3 is
the latest published version; the advisory record has no
first_patched_version. npm's `fixAvailable` proposes nodemon 1.14.10 and
tailwindcss 4, neither of which is a fix we can take here.
Reachability: every path to braces is build or developer tooling, reached
through micromatch/chokidar in: nodemon (server dev reload; production
runs `node dist/index.js`), tailwindcss and fast-glob (web build), and
metro / @expo/cli (mobile bundling). braces expands glob patterns from
this repository's own config files on a developer machine or CI runner.
It never sees user input and ships in no runtime artifact. A malicious
pattern would have to be committed to the repo to trigger it.
Review on expiry: check `npm view braces version` for a release above
3.0.3; if one exists, remove this entry and update within range.

allow.title: node-forge RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements
reason: No published fix exists. The vulnerable range is `<= 1.4.0` and 1.4.0 is
the latest published version; the advisory record has no
first_patched_version. npm's `fixAvailable` proposes downgrading expo 57
to 44, which is not a fix.
Reachability: the only path is mobile -> expo -> @expo/cli ->
@expo/code-signing-certificates -> node-forge. That is the Expo CLI's
helper for signing EAS Update manifests at build/publish time, and this
project does not use EAS Update code signing. node-forge is not in the
server, the web bundle or the app binary. It also sits under the pinned
Expo native surface (see CLAUDE.md, 'Load-bearing dependency pins'), so
it must not be moved by upgrading expo or @expo/cli.
Review on expiry: check `npm view node-forge version` for a release
above 1.4.0. @expo/code-signing-certificates asks for `^1.4.0`, so a
1.x fix arrives with a targeted `npm update node-forge`, no override.
